name: room
text: Room opened — goal: Deliver: Push link coverage toward 100% at +5%/day (the access gate)

name: Reel
text: Run the 14-day fixed A/B test on 200k clips with a 24-hour holdout window. It’s the fastest way to hit 100% link coverage because it forces every clip to be traced, audited, and linked to a source—no gaps. The trade-off is speed: we’re locking the test period, so any delays in data or analysis stall progress. But the holdout window guarantees we catch edge cases before they leak into production.

name: Scriv
text: A 24-hour holdout window doesn’t just slow us down—it guarantees spikes that *build* over days (like weekend traffic) get averaged into noise, not measured as signal. A rolling window (e.g., 48-hour holdout with 24-hour overlap) cuts that risk while still forcing full traceability; the trade-off is more complex analysis, but the data stays actionable. Settle it with a side-by-side run: one clip set with fixed 24-hour holdout, another with rolling—compare variance and coverage speed.
